biography: José Carlos Dias, a name now whispered with anticipation in Brazilian motorsports, hails from the vibrant favelas of Rio de Janeiro. His journey from the dusty, makeshift go-kart tracks of his youth to the polished circuits of professional racing is nothing short of a fairytale. It all started with a discarded engine block and a burning desire to go faster than anyone else. José spent his teenage years hustling and tinkering, building his own kart and challenging anyone brave enough to race him. One sweltering afternoon, a scout from Tepetes Bandeirante spotted his raw talent and fearless overtaking maneuvers. Recognizing his potential, they offered him a spot in their driver development program. Now, at 24, José is making waves in the Brazilian Stock Car series, proving he's more than just a flash in the pan, aiming for international competitions soon.
drivingStyle: José's driving style is as flamboyant as his personality. He's an aggressive overtaker, known for late-braking maneuvers and daring passes that often leave other drivers shaking their heads. While this approach can lead to spectacular results, it also carries risks. He relies heavily on instinct and feel, sometimes sacrificing tire management for raw speed. He thrives under pressure, often finding an extra gear when the stakes are highest. His driving is a high-wire act, a constant dance between brilliance and disaster.

careerHighlight: Winning the Rio de Janeiro Stock Car race in front of his hometown crowd, overtaking three cars on the final lap with a breathtaking move through the Senna S.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the championship-deciding race due to a mechanical failure, costing him his first national title.
